note: THREE GATE RUNS, SAME TREE, AND cpu_ratio IS WHAT TELLS CONTENTION FROM REGRESSION. The Axes ran make gate three times on an unchanged tree. Suite green every time: 3555 passed, 124 skipped, zero failures. timings_alarm went red twice. run 1 cpu_ratio 5.81 wall 501.7s alarmed WHOLE-SUITE at +30 percent while I was building alongside it. run 2 cpu_ratio 7.90 wall 334.2s alarmed PER-TEST on seven unrelated tests across three crates, every one at 2.0 to 2.2x, at loadavg 12.03 on ten cores. run 3 cpu_ratio 8.43 wall 310.9s went GREEN with no other builds running. TWO RULES FALL OUT. First, cpu_ratio is the discriminator: the documented saturating range on this host is 8.25 to 8.50, and a contended run reports LOWER because it achieves less parallelism, while a genuine regression raises wall time at unchanged cpu_ratio. Check cpu_ratio before you believe a duration alarm. Second, A UNIFORM MULTIPLIER IS NOT A PATHOLOGY: run 2 named seven unrelated tests all at the same 2x while advising that something specific went pathological in this test, investigate it directly. That message is well written for the single-test case and actively misleading for the contended one. I nearly investigated hornvale-book. WHAT I RULED OUT FIRST, so the next reader does not have to: the baseline was NOT stale (recorded on this host one commit back, after everything the branch absorbed) and NOT the wrong host file (hostname -s is MacBookPro and that is the file being read, so the new-host free-pass blind spot was not in play). This is blind spot 1 from CLAUDE.md firing for real with numbers attached: the guard asks only whether a census claim is held, so parallel agent sessions are invisible to it. Five worktrees currently exist on a box whose stated working ceiling is two to three. I did NOT re-record the baseline to go green; the green came from a quiet box.
